title: 2023年6月 第2套

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Police have reported a man being bitten by a 4-foot snake when he lifted his toilet seat on Sunday morning.
lines.translation: 警方报告称,周日早晨一名男子在掀开马桶盖时被一条4英尺长的蛇咬伤。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The snake was not poisonous, so the man did not have to go to the hospital, but his arm was medically treated at the scene.
lines.translation: 这条蛇没有毒性,因此该男子无需前往医院,但他的手臂在现场接受了医疗处理。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The police officer interviewed told news reporters the snake didn't belong to the man and it was unclear how it got into the apartment.
lines.translation: 接受采访的警官告诉新闻记者,这条蛇不属于该男子,目前尚不清楚它是如何进入公寓的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The snake was eventually captured by the local animal handlers and taken to an animal hospital afterward.
lines.translation: 这条蛇最终被当地动物处理人员捕获,随后被送往动物医院。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It was being treated for an outer skin infection.
lines.translation: 它正在接受外层皮肤感染的治疗。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It was unclear who the owner was.
lines.translation: 目前尚不清楚主人是谁。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The snake may be taken to a local zoo for care if the owner does not come forward.
lines.translation: 如果主人不出现认领,这条蛇可能会被送到当地动物园照料。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Over the years, other creatures like frogs and fish have found their way into toilets.
lines.translation: 多年来,青蛙和鱼等其他生物也曾以各种方式进入马桶。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But this was the first instance of a snake in recent years.
lines.translation: 但这是近年来首次出现蛇的情况。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 1. What do we learn from the police report?
lines.translation: 第 1 题：我们从警方报告中了解到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 2. What does the report say was still unclear?
lines.translation: 第 2 题：报告称什么仍不清楚?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Every week since last April, Andrea Belcher has been doing something slightly unusual and amusing when she takes out her trash.
lines.translation: 自去年四月以来,每周当Andrea Belcher倒垃圾时,她都会做一件略显不寻常而有趣的事。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It all started off when a movie star shared a photo of herself putting her trash bins out in a ball gown.
lines.translation: 这一切始于一位电影明星分享了一张自己穿着晚礼服倒垃圾的照片。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This inspired Andrea to get dressed up to take out the trash.
lines.translation: 这启发了Andrea盛装打扮去倒垃圾。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: She was too embarrassed to do it during the day.
lines.translation: 她白天不好意思这样做。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So one dark evening, she put on her black off-the-shoulder gown and put her trash bin out.
lines.translation: 所以在一个漆黑的夜晚,她穿上了黑色露肩礼服去倒垃圾桶。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Her daughter filmed it and the whole family laughed, but it seemed to go down well.
lines.translation: 她女儿拍摄了这一幕,全家人都笑了,但效果似乎不错。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The following weeks, she found other outfits in her dressing-up box, and dressed up as different characters and famous people, sharing her exploits on social media.
lines.translation: 接下来的几周,她从自己的装扮箱里找出其他服装,打扮成不同的角色和名人,在社交媒体上分享她的趣事。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Before long, people started offering up their own fancy dresses for her to wear.
lines.translation: 不久之后,人们开始主动提供自己的华丽服装给她穿。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And before she knew it, she had done 20 weeks.
lines.translation: 在她意识到之前,她已经坚持了20周。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Explaining why she has kept up the videos, Andrea explained how nice it was to have a little bit of fun and craziness that made people smile.
lines.translation: 在解释为什么她一直坚持拍摄这些视频时,Andrea说能有一点乐趣和疯狂让人们微笑是多么美好。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Besides, it also helps to remind people in the community to put out their trash bins each week.
lines.translation: 此外,这也有助于提醒社区里的人们每周倒垃圾桶。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 3. What has Andrea Belcher been doing since last April?
lines.translation: 第 3 题：自去年四月以来，Andrea Belcher 一直在做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 4. Why has Andrea Belcher kept up her videos?
lines.translation: 第 4 题：为什么 Andrea Belcher 一直坚持制作她的视频?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: No money but still hungry?
lines.translation: 没钱但仍然饿着？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: No problem!
lines.translation: 没问题！

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Welcome to Frank's restaurant where customers are paying for meals and leaving receipts on a board.
lines.translation: 欢迎来到Frank's餐厅，这里的顾客为餐食付款后会把收据留在一块板子上。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Anyone who is hungry and wants something to eat can take one, no questions asked and hand it to the staff for some food.
lines.translation: 任何饿了想吃东西的人都可以拿走一张，无需回答任何问题，然后把它交给工作人员换取食物。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The idea for the board of free meals started after a donor came in with $100 for each member of its staff.
lines.translation: 免费餐食板的想法始于一位捐赠者带着100美元来给每位员工。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: After two staffers returned to their share, there was $700 leftover according to Tarah Morris, the owner of the restaurant, so they decided to do something more by creating the board.
lines.translation: 据餐厅老板Tarah Morris说,两名员工退还了他们的份额后,还剩下700美元,于是他们决定通过创建这块板子来做更多的事情。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The board of free meals inside the restaurant shows a host of potential meals already paid for by customers, each costing about $10.
lines.translation: 餐厅内免费膳食的董事会显示,顾客已经支付了大量潜在的膳食费用,每餐费用约为10美元。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The board has messages of kindness like, "If you want more kindness in the world, put it here."
lines.translation: 董事会有善意的讯息,比如, "如果你想要 更多的善在世界上,把它放在这里。"

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The drive has been going on for two weeks and Morris said just under 50 customers have picked up a free meal.
lines.translation: 这项活动已经进行了两周,Morris说有将近50位顾客领取了免费餐食。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: There have been no reports of anyone taking advantage of the situation.
lines.translation: 没有任何人利用这种情况的报告。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In fact, there are a lot more people giving tickets than receiving.
lines.translation: 事实上,给予餐券的人比领取的人多得多。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It seems people want to help and are driven by helping others.
lines.translation: 似乎人们想要帮助他人,并被帮助他人所驱动。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 5. What can people do at Frank's restaurant?
lines.translation: 第 5 题：人们在Frank餐厅可以做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 6. What does the owner of the restaurant say about the idea for the board of free meals?
lines.translation: 第 6 题：餐厅老板对免费餐食公告板这个想法是怎么说的?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 7. What has happened at Frank's restaurant since the board of free meals was created?
lines.translation: 第 7 题：自从免费餐食公告板创建以来,Frank餐厅发生了什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Conversation one.
lines.translation: 交谈之一。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Welcome to our program, friends and relationships.
lines.translation: 欢迎来到我们的节目《朋友与关系》。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Our guest today is psychologist Steve Pinker from McGill University.
lines.translation: 我们今天的嘉宾是来自McGill大学的心理学家Steve Pinker。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Glad to be here, Jane.
lines.translation: 很高兴来到这里,Jane。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Hi, Steve.
lines.translation: 你好,Steve。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Our question today is why friends suddenly disappear.
lines.translation: 我们今天的问题是为什么朋友会突然消失。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They may block us on their social media accounts and stop responding to our emails.
lines.translation: 他们可能会在社交媒体账号上屏蔽我们,不再回复我们的邮件。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They simply vanish without a trace.
lines.translation: 他们就这样消失得无影无踪。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The answer may lie in childhood, the way the person related to their mom and dad.
lines.translation: 答案可能在于童年时期,也就是这个人与父母相处的方式。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's related to their attachment styles.
lines.translation: 这与他们的依恋类型有关。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Attachment styles?
lines.translation: 依恋类型?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Yeah.
lines.translation: 是的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: There are two different attachment styles: an anxious attachment style and an avoidant attachment style.
lines.translation: 有两种不同的依恋类型:焦虑型依恋和回避型依恋。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: When there is a relationship breakdown with their parents, children with an anxious attachment style scream and cry to get their parents to come back.
lines.translation: 当与父母的关系破裂时,焦虑型依恋的孩子会又哭又闹,想让父母回来。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But other children simply shut down and try to deal with their emotions by ignoring the situation.
lines.translation: 但另一些孩子只是封闭自己,试图通过忽视这种情况来处理自己的情绪。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And these attachment styles carry on into adulthood.
lines.translation: 而这些依恋类型会延续到成年期。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Does avoidance reduce their stress levels?
lines.translation: 回避能降低他们的压力水平吗?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Not really.
lines.translation: 并不能。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Their stress levels are actually the same as those experienced by the children who yell and scream.
lines.translation: 他们的压力水平实际上和那些大喊大叫的孩子经历的压力水平是一样的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And I assume both might be termed insecure.
lines.translation: 我猜这两种都可以被称为不安全型。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Exactly.
lines.translation: 完全正确。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And it's a very insecure attachment.
lines.translation: 这是一种非常不安全的依恋。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: How does an insecure attachment affect relationships between friends, co-workers and romantic relationships?
lines.translation: 不安全型依恋如何影响朋友之间、同事之间以及恋爱关系?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's the same as conflicts.
lines.translation: 和冲突的情况一样。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So if you have a disagreement with a securely attached person, they're not going to panic.
lines.translation: 所以如果你和一个安全型依恋的人产生分歧,他们不会惊慌失措。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They're able to hear what the other person is saying and express their own feelings and thoughts effectively.
lines.translation: 他们能够听进对方在说什么,并有效地表达自己的感受和想法。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: However, an insecurely attached person won't.
lines.translation: 然而,不安全型依恋的人不会这样。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They might either attack you, get defensive, or just disappear from your life.
lines.translation: 他们可能会攻击你,变得防御性很强,或者直接从你的生活中消失。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: To them, a difference, no matter how small in your eyes, signals the end of the relationship.
lines.translation: 对他们来说,分歧,无论在你眼中多么微小,都预示着关系的终结。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That explains why they suddenly disappear.
lines.translation: 这就解释了为什么他们会突然消失。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 8. What do we learn about the man?
lines.translation: 第 8 题：关于这位男士我们了解到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 9. What are the speakers mainly talking about?
lines.translation: 第 9 题：说话者主要在谈论什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 10. How do children with an anxious attachment style react to a breakdown in their relationship with parents?
lines.translation: 第 10 题：具有焦虑型依恋风格的儿童如何应对与父母关系的破裂?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 11. What does the man say about insecurely attached people?
lines.translation: 第 11 题：这位男士关于不安全依恋型的人说了什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Conversation 2.
lines.translation: 对话2。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I hear you're going to Japan soon.
lines.translation: 我听说你快要去日本了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Yes, that's right.
lines.translation: 是的，没错。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Could I ask you a favor?
lines.translation: 我能请你帮个忙吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Sure.
lines.translation: 当然可以。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What is it?
lines.translation: 什么事？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I was wondering if you could get me some jeans while you're there.
lines.translation: 我在想你在那儿的时候能不能帮我买条牛仔裤。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I'll pay you back, of course.
lines.translation: 当然我会还你钱的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: A pair of jeans?
lines.translation: 一条牛仔裤？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Okay.
lines.translation: 好吧。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I don't see why not.
lines.translation: 我觉得没问题。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But what's wrong with jeans here?
lines.translation: 但这里的牛仔裤有什么不好吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Well, I just love good jeans and Japan happens to make the best in the world.
lines.translation: 嗯，我就是喜欢好牛仔裤，而日本恰好生产世界上最好的牛仔裤。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: My friend brought me a pair from there five years ago, and they still look new.
lines.translation: 我朋友五年前从那儿给我带了一条，现在看起来还跟新的一样。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Really?
lines.translation: 真的吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I had no idea Japan made jeans.
lines.translation: 我完全不知道日本还生产牛仔裤。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I would have thought America made the best jeans because it's a typical American garment.
lines.translation: 我还以为美国生产最好的牛仔裤呢，因为这是典型的美国服装。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Yeah, I thought so too.
lines.translation: 是啊，我也是这么想的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But it turns out Japan still has some very old mills with the traditional weaving tools used to make jeans the original way.
lines.translation: 但事实证明日本仍然有一些非常古老的工厂，使用传统的织布工具以原始方式制作牛仔裤。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's a slower process of making clothing.
lines.translation: 这是一种比较慢的服装制作工艺。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But the end result is surely superior.
lines.translation: 但最终成品绝对更优质。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Also, the fabric they use is of a higher quality and the dyes are natural.
lines.translation: 而且，他们使用的面料质量更高，染料也是天然的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They have a denser weave, and are more durable than any other jeans in the world.
lines.translation: 织得更密实，比世界上任何其他牛仔裤都更耐用。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That sounds cool.
lines.translation: 听起来不错。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What size do you want and how much are they?
lines.translation: 你要什么尺码的，多少钱？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I have a 34 waist and size 30 or 32 in length.
lines.translation: 我腰围34，长度30或32都行。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Either is fine.
lines.translation: 哪个都可以。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They should be around $500.
lines.translation: 大概500美元左右。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But make double certain they are made in Japan.
lines.translation: 但一定要再三确认是日本制造的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Boy, that's expensive.
lines.translation: 天哪，太贵了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Do you typically spend that much on a pair of casual trousers?
lines.translation: 你平时买休闲裤都花这么多钱吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They are a little pricey, yes.
lines.translation: 确实是有点贵。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But they are very special.
lines.translation: 但它们很特别。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Bear in mind, they will last me several years and they're very fashionable too.
lines.translation: 要知道，它们能穿好几年，而且也很时尚。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I think they're totally worth it.
lines.translation: 我觉得完全值得。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 12. What makes the man choose to buy jeans made in Japan?
lines.translation: 第 12 题：是什么让这位男士选择购买日本制造的牛仔裤?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 13. Why is the woman puzzled by the man's request?
lines.translation: 第 13 题：为什么这位女士对男士的要求感到困惑?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 14. What does the man say about the dyes of Japanese jeans?
lines.translation: 第 14 题：关于日本牛仔裤的染料,男士说了什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 15. What does the man say about Japanese jeans at the end of the conversation?
lines.translation: 第 15 题：在对话结束时,男士对日本牛仔裤说了什么?

lines.translation: 在答题单单行的答题表一中标出相应的字母。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Every time I walk out of a superhero movie, I feel the same way.
lines.translation: 每次走出超级英雄电影院，我都有同样的感受。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I experience a sense of longing, realizing that there should be more in life.
lines.translation: 我体验到一种渴望感，意识到生活中应该有更多东西。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The desire for adventure is a human one.
lines.translation: 对冒险的渴望是人类共有的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Superhero films capture this desire perfectly.
lines.translation: 超级英雄电影完美地捕捉了这种渴望。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The plot of each superhero film has become relatively predictable: the world is in peril, the world needs a hero, the hero is in peril, the hero resolves the peril, the hero saves the world.
lines.translation: 每部超级英雄电影的情节都变得相对可预测：世界陷入危险，世界需要英雄，英雄陷入危险，英雄化解危险，英雄拯救世界。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Each film has an attractive lead, several expensive explosions, a few jokes to lighten the mood, and numerous punches that land unrealistically well.
lines.translation: 每部电影都有一个有魅力的主角、几场昂贵的爆炸、一些缓和气氛的笑话，以及无数不切实际地精准命中的拳头。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Even though we basically know what will happen, we keep coming back for more.
lines.translation: 尽管我们基本上知道会发生什么，我们还是不断回来观看更多。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The elites of our society have rejected superhero films.
lines.translation: 我们社会的精英阶层排斥超级英雄电影。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They say the films lack any form of artistry.
lines.translation: 他们说这些电影缺乏任何形式的艺术性。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: These movies are criticized as being too simple.
lines.translation: 这些电影被批评为过于简单。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But they give the fans what they want—entertainment.
lines.translation: 但它们给粉丝想要的东西——娱乐。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: No matter the form in which they reveal themselves, hero stories will always be present in life.
lines.translation: 无论他们以何种形式露面,英雄故事都会在生活中出现。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's not just about being entertained, but also being inspired.
lines.translation: 不只是娱乐,还有灵感

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: One author has mentioned that women desire to play an irreplaceable role in a great adventure.
lines.translation: 一位作者提到,妇女希望在一次伟大的冒险中发挥不可替代的作用。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: "Most young women want to be a part of something grand, something important." It seems clear that this principle applies to men, as well.
lines.translation: 多数年轻女性想成为重要的东西的一部分。 似乎很明显,这个原则也适用于男性。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So next time you see your favorite superhero film, be entertained, but also be inspired.
lines.translation: 所以下次你观看最喜欢的超级英雄电影时，享受娱乐，但也要受到激励。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Let that small longing you feel motivate you to make a difference.
lines.translation: 让你感受到的那种微小渴望激励你去做出改变。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Question 16-18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
lines.translation: 问题16-18是基于你刚才听到的段落。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 16. How does the speaker feel every time he walks out of a superhero movie?
lines.translation: 第 16 题：说话者每次走出超级英雄电影院时感觉如何？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 17. What does the passage say about the plot of all superhero movies?
lines.translation: 第 17 题：文章关于所有超级英雄电影的情节是怎么说的？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 18. What do the elites of American society think of superhero movies?
lines.translation: 第 18 题：美国社会的精英阶层对超级英雄电影有什么看法？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Telling stories is one of the most powerful means leaders have to influence, teach,
lines.translation: 讲故事是领袖们 影响、教、教、教

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Storytelling forges connections among people.
lines.translation: 讲故事能在人与人之间建立联系。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: When it comes to our countries, our communities, and our families, we understand instinctively that the stories we hold in common are an important part of the ties that bind.
lines.translation: 当涉及我们的国家、我们的社区和我们的家庭时,我们本能地理解,我们共同拥有的故事是维系彼此纽带的重要组成部分。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This understanding also holds true in the business world, where an organization's stories, and the stories its leaders tell, help solidify relationships in a way that factual statements don't.
lines.translation: 这种理解在商业世界中同样适用,在那里,一个组织的故事以及其领导者讲述的故事,能以一种事实陈述所无法做到的方式帮助巩固关系。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Good stories do more than create a sense of connection.
lines.translation: 好的故事不仅仅能创造一种联系感。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They build familiarity and trust.
lines.translation: 它们建立熟悉感和信任。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They allow the listener to enter the story, making them more open to learning.
lines.translation: 它们让听众进入故事之中,使他们更愿意学习。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Good stories can contain multiple meanings, so they're surprisingly economical in conveying complex ideas in graspable ways.
lines.translation: 好的故事可以包含多重含义,因此它们在以可理解的方式传达复杂思想方面出人意料地经济高效。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And stories are more engaging than the recital of data points or a discussion of abstract ideas.
lines.translation: 而且故事比罗列数据点或讨论抽象概念更具吸引力。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Stories about professional mistakes and what leaders learned from them are another great avenue for learning.
lines.translation: 关于职业错误以及领导者从中学到的经验的故事是另一条很好的学习途径。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Because people identify so closely with stories, they can imagine how they would have acted in similar circumstances.
lines.translation: 因为人们与故事产生如此紧密的认同,他们可以想象自己在类似情况下会如何行动。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They're able to work through situations in a way that's risk-free.
lines.translation: 他们能够以一种零风险的方式来处理各种情境。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: There are extra benefits for leaders: with a simple personal story, they can convey fundamental values.
lines.translation: 对领导者来说还有额外的好处:通过一个简单的个人故事,他们可以传达基本价值观。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They can offer insight into the evolution of their own experience and knowledge, presenting themselves as more approachable and then they are more likely to inspire others to want to know more.
lines.translation: 他们可以深入展现自己经验和知识的演变过程,使自己显得更平易近人,从而更有可能激发他人想要了解更多的愿望。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 19. What does the passage say about storytelling?
lines.translation: 第 19 题：文章关于讲故事说了什么？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 20. What can good stories do to listeners according to the passage?
lines.translation: 第 20 题：根据文章，好的故事能对听众产生什么作用？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 21. What can leaders do with a simple personal story?
lines.translation: 第 21 题：领导者可以用一个简单的个人故事做什么？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Passage 3,
lines.translation: 通行证3号,

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: the US was founded by successive waves of immigrants and immigrants are still contributing to America today.
lines.translation: 美国是由一波波波波的移民和移民建立的, 移民今天仍在为美国作出贡献。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: was founded by successive waves of immigrants, and immigrants are still contributing to America today—statistics prove it.
lines.translation: 移民仍为美国贡献力量, 统计家们证明了这一点。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: On two key measures of financial performance, immigrants outperform native-born Americans.
lines.translation: 在衡量财务表现的两个关键指标上,移民的表现优于本土出生的美国人。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: First, they are more likely to be entrepreneurs.
lines.translation: 首先,他们更有可能成为企业家。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: From 1996 to 2016, the pace at which immigrants started businesses was double that of U.S.-born individuals.
lines.translation: 从1996年至2016年,移民开办企业的速度是美国出生个人两倍。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Immigrants aren't just becoming entrepreneurs more frequently.
lines.translation: 移民不仅更经常地成为企业家。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They're often succeeding.
lines.translation: 他们经常成功

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Over 40% of Fortune 500 companies had a founder who was either an immigrant or the child of one.
lines.translation: 40%以上的《财富》500家公司的创始人要么是移民,要么是一子。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Another key measure of financial strength is debt level.
lines.translation: 衡量财政实力的另一个关键尺度是债务水平。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Immigrants do better in this area too.
lines.translation: 移民在这方面也做得更好。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Immigrants use credit less often for purchasing cars, homes or starting businesses.
lines.translation: 移民较少利用信贷购买汽车、住宅或创办企业。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This results in significantly lower levels of debt than native-born Americans.
lines.translation: 这导致债务水平大大低于原生美国人。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: For example, 34% of Americans born in Latin America report no credit card or installment loan debt.
lines.translation: 例如,在拉丁美洲出生的美国人中,34%没有报告信用卡或分期付款贷款债务。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This can be compared to just 19% of the general population.
lines.translation: 这与总人口中只有19%相比。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Why are immigrants doing so well?
lines.translation: 移民为什么做得这么好?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The values and habits they bring from their own homelands help explain some of the success.
lines.translation: 他们从自己家园带来的价值观和习惯有助于解释一些成功。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Unemployment tends to be higher in developing countries.
lines.translation: 发展中国家的失业率往往较高。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That means more people must become entrepreneurs.
lines.translation: 这意味着更多的人必须成为企业家。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Credit is also scarcer in most developing countries.
lines.translation: 在大多数发展中国家,信贷也较稀少。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This means individuals must save more in order to achieve their goals, or they borrow money from friends and family rather than a bank.
lines.translation: 这意味着个人必须储蓄更多,以实现其目标,或者向朋友和家人而不是银行借钱。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That means less debt and potentially better credit outcomes when they reach the U.S.
lines.translation: 这意味着债务减少,当它们到达美国时,信贷结果可能更好。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the passage you have just heard.
lines.translation: 问题22至25是基于你刚才听到的段落。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 22. What does the passage say statistics prove?
lines.translation: 第 22 题：文章说统计数据证明了什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 23. What do we learn about immigrants in the U.S., compared with native-born Americans?
lines.translation: 第 23 题：与在美国出生的美国人相比,我们对美国移民了解到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 24. What does the passage say about immigrants in the U.S., in terms of financial strength?
lines.translation: 第 24 题：就财务实力而言,文章对美国移民说了什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 25. What do immigrants do to achieve their goals in the U.S.?
lines.translation: 第 25 题：移民在美国做什么来实现他们的目标?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: the end of listening comprehension.
lines.translation: 听力理解的结束
